name: manual_cabdd0
claim: A deny-by-default SSRF transport needs an explicit opposite-polarity local/LAN path for its own default deployment target, or that default target becomes permanently unreachable in production

decisions.notes: orchestrator/orama_bridge.py routed every call -- including the default ORAMA_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:8001 -- through ssrf_request, whose default policy denies loopback/RFC1918 by design. Every real call to orama's own default deployment would raise AddressDenied; existing tests never caught it because they mocked ssrf_request entirely, silently absorbing the loopback case (a false green). Fixed by classifying local (loopback/RFC1918) vs remote via validate_model_endpoint_url(url, allow_public=False) and routing local traffic through a direct httpx call, mirroring connectivity.py's proven _probe/_probe_local split. General pattern: whenever a Layer-2 SSRF adapter is the default transport for a service, check whether that service's OWN default endpoint falls inside the adapter's deny range -- if so it needs the opposite-polarity path, not a blanket allow-all. Landed as PT commit 92259e6f (2026-08-23), fixing CodeRabbit discussion_r3834992455 (PT PR #359 'Deferred #2').
